o: Recognise what an IP address and MAC address identify.
Explain why switches use MAC addresses and routers use IP addresses.
Identify simple examples of IPv4 and MAC-address formats.
c: An IP address identifies a network destination and allows routers to forward traffic between networks. IPv4 is commonly shown as four decimal numbers.
A MAC address identifies a network interface; it is commonly shown as six pairs of hexadecimal digits.
Within a LAN, switches forward based on MAC addresses. Between networks, routers use IP addresses.
IPv4 and MAC addresses have different roles and formats. Do not confuse a device's IP address with the MAC address of its NIC.

m.title: A message leaves the school
m.q: A computer sends data to a website on another network. Explain why both MAC and IP addressing may be used. [4 marks]
st: The computer first communicates on its local network, then needs to reach a remote network.
Local network interfaces use MAC addresses [1], allowing switching towards the local gateway [1].
Routers use IP addresses [1] to forward data between networks towards the destination [1].
Match four points to local MAC use and remote IP routing.

w: A printer and PC share one LAN. Explain why MAC addresses are useful to a switch. [4 marks]
A network interface has a MAC address [1] identifying it locally [1]. A switch uses MAC addresses [1] to direct traffic to the intended LAN port/device [1].
A college connects its LAN to an external website. Explain how IP addresses support the connection. [4 marks]
Destination IP address identifies the remote network destination [1]. Routers inspect IP addressing [1] and forward packets between networks [1] towards the correct server [1].
A technician sees 10.2.4.8 and 5A:01:2B:0C:34:EF. Compare these two addresses. [4 marks]
10.2.4.8 is IPv4 [1] shown as four decimal values [1]. 5A:01:2B:0C:34:EF is a MAC address [1], shown as six hexadecimal pairs [1].
wSteps: Focus on local device identification, not Internet routing.
MAC identifies an interface [2]; switch reads that address [1].
Traffic is delivered to the intended LAN device [1].
A network interface has a MAC address [1] identifying it locally [1]. A switch uses MAC addresses [1] to direct traffic to the intended LAN port/device [1].
Start with destination address, then describe what the router does.
IP identifies network destination [1]; router uses the address [1].
Data can travel between networks [1] towards the correct host [1].
Destination IP address identifies the remote network destination [1]. Routers inspect IP addressing [1] and forward packets between networks [1] towards the correct server [1].
Look at punctuation, decimal octets and hexadecimal pairs.
10.2.4.8 is IPv4 [1] shown as four decimal values [1]. 5A:01:2B:0C:34:EF is a MAC address [1], shown as six hexadecimal pairs [1].

k.q: Select whether to print an IP or MAC example for a local or remote destination.
k.code:
remote = 1
if remote > 0 then
    print("Use destination IP")
else
    print("Use local MAC")
endif
p: Add print("Address checked") after the IF statement.
k.a:
Original: Use destination IP. Changed: Use local MAC.

Extended OCR ERL:
remote = 0
if remote > 0 then
    print("Use destination IP")
else
    print("Use local MAC")
endif
print("Address checked")

Outputs: Use local MAC; Address checked. This is a simplified teaching model.
